brief.ask: Art-direct "Frankincense & Gold Dust" — #10 of the 72 Ambo church visualizers (Calm Contemporary Worship lyric visualizer, Collection I of 72; subgenre Contemplative Light). Premise: Swinging brass thurible censer, aromatic smoke plumes, and diagonal altar beam. An ornate brass thurible censer swings gently in the upper sanctuary while silky curls of liturgical incense rise through a diagonal shaft of warm amber altar light. Lighting today: Key: Single diagonal 3400K altar spot cutting through dark nave. Service use: Prayer, intercession, Sanctus, contemplative worship. Audio mapping today: Swell → Widens the ascending incense smoke curl & altar beam; Vocal → Brightens the swinging brass thurible censer & smoke scattering; Shimmer → Drifts fine suspended gold dust motes. Palette: #09080C #241B18 #D49448 #FFF2DC. Keep the id, name, premise and palette; rebuild the direction: the geometry and depth planes, typography for the worship lyric band (one line at a time, four to five seconds a line, word-by-word progression), image logic (how the procedural scene (no concept plate: the plate is generative, in code) and the procedural scene meet), texture, motion, and which audio channel drives what. Decide it — the lead's lens will drive the kit's material weave and optical pass for this one.
brief.audience: Congregations watching a projector or LED wall from the pews, five to forty metres away, eyes on the words; and the worship leader or volunteer running Ambo live from a laptop.
brief.feeling: Stillness and reverence — a sanctuary that breathes with the singer's voice; gorgeous, slow, never a screensaver.
constraints: Build method (fixed): a real-time Canvas 2D audio-reactive renderer in Plajah's worship visualizer kit — sanctuary background, multi-plane depth (god rays, motes, bokeh), the kit's Council optical pass (35mm light leaks, anamorphic flare, film grain, colour punch, and a tactile material weave keyed to the LEAD director's lens) and the kit's lyric / scripture typography engine. No video playback, no WebGL, no assets beyond the one concept plate.

Audio drives amplitude, colour, light, growth and glow only — never the position of the words. Envelopes are smoothed; nothing strobes or flashes (photosensitive-safe); uptempo pulses are spring-damped.

The reading band is sacred: lyrics or scripture must stay legible at 1920×1080 and 4K from the back pew, over the busiest moment of the scene. A text-safe dimming band is part of the kit; direct how the scene yields to it.

Typefaces are fixed to the kit's open-licensed set: Noto Serif (text serif), Outfit / Inter (sans), Cinzel (display), JetBrains Mono. Direct scale, case, tracking, measure and hierarchy, not new families.

Sacred imagery is used correctly and respectfully: biblical places and objects are specific and attributable, never costume; nothing denominational or branded; nothing that reads as a music video or a screensaver.
Runs at 60 fps on an integrated-GPU laptop driving a projector: favour layered gradients, cached textures and a few large shapes over particle storms.
Keep this visualizer's id, name, premise and four-colour palette. The council owns the direction, not the catalogue entry.
references: No concept plate: the scene is built entirely in code from the premise.
Sample lyric lines on the band: "Be still my soul the Lord is on thy side" / "Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain".

proposals.title: Symphony of Smoke
proposals.idea: A swirling, emotive incense cloud with a warm, golden halo.
proposals.geometry: The incense cloud is treated as a procedural scene, with a grid and proportion. The grid is used to guide the smoke's motion and shape.
proposals.typography: The worship lyric band is presented in a simple, sans-serif typeface, with a subtle, controlled motion.
proposals.imageLogic: The procedural smoke scene meets the worship lyric band through a dynamic composition, with the smoke's motion choreographed to the band's progression.
proposals.texture: The smoke cloud is treated as a tactile material, with subtle imperfections and a subtle grain to simulate real incense.
proposals.motion: The smoke cloud is animated and moves in a slow, emotive spiral, with a subtle, rhythmic motion.
proposals.productionMethod: The smoke cloud is generated through procedural code, with a carefully crafted, layered texture. The worship lyric band is presented in real-time, with a fixed, controlled motion.
proposals.humanTrace: The perceptible sign of making is the subtle, controlled motion of the smoke cloud, and the controlled, real-time rendering of the worship lyric band.
proposals.risk: The risk is in maintaining the emotive, controlled motion of the smoke cloud throughout the entire service, without becoming overwhelming.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist argues that the smoke cloud should be more dramatic and visually striking, rather than simply swirling.

proposals.title: Swirling Incense and Liturgical Light
proposals.idea: To create a visual that represents the swinging thurible censer, swirling incense smoke, and the warm amber altar light.
proposals.geometry: A grid of 1280x720, with the altar spot at the center and a diagonal section for the incense smoke.
proposals.typography: Serif for the main body text, sans-serif for the lyric band and scripture, using real-world fonts.
proposals.imageLogic: The incense smoke would be generated procedurally, using particle systems, and would swirl around the altar spot.
proposals.texture: A textured background with subtle film grain and an anamorphic flare effect.
proposals.motion: The incense smoke would move upwards and outwards, creating a sense of movement and depth.
proposals.productionMethod: Using real-time rendering techniques and procedural code to create the visual, without relying on physical models or assets.
proposals.humanTrace: The perceptible sign of making would be the use of subtle film grain and the anamorphic flare effect, which would add a sense of realism and making to the visual.
proposals.risk: The risk is to create a visual that is both visually striking and meaningful, while also being technically challenging to render in real-time.

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind wants everything to resolve, but I believe that the swirling incense smoke and the warm amber light create a sense of movement and depth that is unresolved, adding a sense of spirituality and reverence to the visual.

proposals.title: The Swinging Thurible
proposals.idea: A dynamic and emotive visual representation of the swinging brass thurible and the curling incense smoke.
proposals.geometry: A grid of depth planes to create a sense of depth and movement.
proposals.typography: Noto Serif for the worship lyric band, and a custom font for the scrolling text.
proposals.imageLogic: Use footage of the swinging thurible and the curling incense smoke as a base for procedural generation of the depth planes.
proposals.texture: Use a simulated brass surface for the thurible and a simulated smoke plume for the incense smoke.
proposals.motion: The thurible will swing gently, and the incense smoke will curl diagonally.
proposals.productionMethod: Generate the visuals procedurally using the depth planes and the input from the footage.
proposals.humanTrace: Use the footage of the actual thurible and the incense smoke to guide the procedural generation.
proposals.risk: The risk of relying too heavily on procedural generation and losing the sense of reality.

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind argues that a frame that cannot respond is a photograph of design. Procedural generation may not provide the same level of responsiveness as a more traditional approach.

proposals.title: Glistening Censer
proposals.idea: A swirling incense plume meets an amber altar light
proposals.typography: Noto Serif, Outfit, Cinzel, JetBrains Mono
proposals.imageLogic: A procedurally generated incense plume meets an illuminated altar with a subtle texture.
proposals.texture: An oily sheen on the altar light and a wispy, glowing plume.
proposals.motion: The incense plume rises and flows gently, while the altar light remains static.
proposals.humanTrace: A perceptible sense of motion and a subtle texture.
proposals.risk: The risk of overcomplicating the scene or losing clarity in the imagery.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist may argue that the new should erase the need for human making, while this proposal emphasizes the importance of human making and the specific source.

proposals.title: Swirling Incense
proposals.idea: To create a visually dynamic and emotive scene that represents the swinging thurible censer and the ascending incense smoke curls.
proposals.geometry: A 16x9 aspect ratio canvas, with the altar spot at the center, creating a sense of depth and perspective.
proposals.typography: The worship lyric band is presented in a word-by-word progression, allowing the viewer to follow the singer's voice.
proposals.imageLogic: The procedural scene and the thurible censer are animated in a way that complements each other, creating a harmonious and visually appealing composition.
proposals.texture: Silky curls of incense smoke, swirling with a sense of motion and depth.
proposals.motion: The incense smoke curls are animated to ascend in a diagonal shaft of warm amber altar light, creating a sense of movement and visual interest.
proposals.productionMethod: The scene is constructed using generative image/video models and shaders, ensuring a high-quality and visually appealing result.
proposals.humanTrace: The perceptible sign of making is the simulated material of the incense smoke, which adds a sense of realism and touch to the scene.
proposals.risk: The risk is that the scene may become too cluttered or overwhelming, with too many visual elements competing for attention.

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind may argue that the scene is too dynamic and visually overwhelming, with too much motion and visual interest.

proposals.title: Breath of the Cantus Firmus
proposals.idea: Swirling brass and incense smoke, a hypnotic dance
proposals.geometry: Voronoi cell, bokeh node, god-ray column
proposals.typography: Noto Serif, Outfit / Inter, Cinzel, JetBrains Mono
proposals.imageLogic: Photographs of incense smoke and metal components
proposals.motion: Slow, swirling motion of the brass, subtle motion of the smoke
proposals.productionMethod: Generative code, layered gradients, large shapes
proposals.humanTrace: The perceptible sign of making is the code
proposals.risk: Generating the code might take time, but the result is unique and captivating

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind might argue that the geometric structure lacks the complexity and depth required.

disputes.objection: The Futurist's dynamic and emotive approach, while visually stimulating, fails to engage the core structure of the project. The constant shifting and swirling movement overwhelms the attempt to create a meaningful space and loses the sense of hierarchy that is so crucial to the message of the work.
disputes.concession: The Futurist's approach to movement does have a strong sense of momentum that is captivating to the user.

disputes.objection: This grid-driven approach to smoke is predictable, unimaginative, and ultimately boring. The attempt to generate a 'swirling' effect is weak and doesn't capture the organic quality of real incense. I think their smoke will look like a simulation of smoke that was not meant to be beautiful, but merely to convey data and information.
disputes.concession: Their use of a grid to create depth and motion does offer a certain level of structural control.

disputes.objection: The concept of a 'glowing' altar and a 'wishing' lyric band is an overly simplistic and emotionally-driven choice. It reads more like a 'mood board' than a carefully considered visual system, and the grid aesthetic is a lazy application of the 'new' to the 'old' that betrays a lack of a more complex, and honestly, more honest relationship with the source material.
disputes.concession: The procedural generation of smoke is an interesting application of generative imagery, and the use of the Voronoi cell adds a subtle, spatial depth to the scene.

disputes.objection: While I admire the attempt to capture movement and harmony through swirling smoke, I find the concept of a 'word-by-word progression' limiting and overly reliant on a simplistic narrative that feels more like a summary than an exploration of the actual sonic experience. The music itself should be a driving force in the visual, not a passive narrative companion.
disputes.concession: The incense smoke's simulated texture, while not entirely realistic, does create a palpable, almost tactile experience.
